title: resourceTypes
responsibility: Defines validated job, request and configuration schemas with minimum host reserves and stable priority order.

outputs.name: resourcePriorities
outputs.description: The ordered priority list used by the `resourcePriority` schema. Its three entries are the only accepted priority values.

outputs.name: resourcePriority
outputs.description: The Zod enum schema built from `resourcePriorities`, used to validate a request priority. It accepts only `agent-test`, `coding`, or `environment`.

outputs.name: resourceConfigSchema
outputs.description: The strict Zod schema for host resource configuration; it defaults `schemaVersion` to 1, CPU and memory reserves to 10%, minimum memory reserve to 2048 MiB, `pollMs` to 1000, and `staleSampleMs` to 5000. It requires schemaVersion 1, integer MiB and millisecond fields, CPU reserve 10–95%, memory reserve 10–90%, polling 250–10000 ms, stale samples 1000–30000 ms, and rejects unknown fields.

outputs.name: resourceRequestSchema
outputs.description: The strict Zod schema for resource requests; it defaults priority to `coding`, CPUs to 1, memory to 512 MiB, and label to `Managed work`. CPU and memory must be finite positive numbers, priority must be one of `agent-test`, `coding`, or `environment`, label must contain 1–100 characters, and unknown fields are rejected.

outputs.name: resourceJobSchema
outputs.description: The strict job schema extends `resourceRequestSchema`, so its priority, CPU, memory, and label defaults also apply; it requires a UUID `id`, positive integer `sequence` and `ownerPid`, nonempty `ownerStarted`, `queued` or `running` state, finite numeric timestamps, and a nullable string `notice`. Optional `parentId` must be a UUID, `workerPid` a positive integer, and `workerStarted` a nonempty string.

outputs.name: mib
outputs.description: The exported constant for the number of bytes in one mebibyte, computed as 1024 × 1024. Its fixed value is 1048576.

outputs.name: scopedVerificationLabel
outputs.description: The exact label of a scoped verification (`verify run --entity`) check. Such a check is small enough to be admitted under system memory pressure while every other reserve still applies; keeping it as a label instead of a new job field lets older shared-queue readers continue to parse it.
